segments.title: Chương 136: Hỏa lực chi viện liên tục
segments.content:
Chapter 139: 0136 Continuous Follow-up Firepower (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader toydemon)

After the writer Lao Gui furiously blasted *Wolf Totem*, Chen Guiliang immediately updated his blog.

This time, he didn't write any critical essays, but instead reposted his poem, *Ode to the Boundless Sea*.

In this era, blogs didn't have a follower function yet, so the main metric was the number of clicks on each article.

A single article with over 100,000 clicks was considered a viral hit.

A click count between 50,000 and 80,000 also made one a top-tier blogger.

Last year, Chen Guiliang had serialized *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* on both "Blog China" and "BlogBus." On the former, each post received over ten thousand clicks, while on the latter, it was only two to three thousand.

Recently, Chen Guiliang had published two critiques of *Wolf Totem*. The first article had already surpassed 80,000 clicks, and the second had over 50,000—this specifically referred to the click counts on Blog China.

Now, Chen Guiliang began his new post by quoting Lao Gui, furiously denouncing *Wolf Totem* for encouraging Chinese people to be traitors. He then posted the full text of his *Ode to the Boundless Sea*.

Just a few minutes later, netizen comments started to appear.

"I finally understand why the blogger is slamming *Wolf Totem*. Even from the humble wilderness, he possesses the spirit to support the heavens and prop up the earth!"

"This damn book deserves to be slammed! I have a moronic classmate who's been spewing nonsense every day since reading *Wolf Totem*. I took a look at it myself and was utterly disgusted. And a whole bunch of newspapers and celebrities are still kissing its ass."

"A while ago, when the media was ganging up on the blogger, I was worried he'd get scared and back down. It looks like he's fine, haha. Is he using his own poem as a call to arms?"

"'The Ninth Heaven's gales tear at my wings, yet I clutch a lone branch, refusing to break. Plunging into the abyss, a hundred fathoms deep, black waves like mountains crash down from above. The stars, inverted, are reflected in a cup of water, heaven and earth flip before my eyes.' Looking at the public opinion from a while ago and now, these lines are so fitting."

"Is this the blogger's own poem?"

"Poster above, you didn't know? The blogger wrote this in high school for a writing competition."

"So talented!"

"Some of the educated youth from back then are already digging up dirt on the author of *Wolf Totem* on the Tianya forum. The guy was a young Red Guard leader at 20 and didn't do anything proper on the grasslands."

"Chen Guiliang is just a huge idiot, leeching off the popularity of *Wolf Totem* because it sells well. His own book reads like a primary school student's essay!"

"Haha, another dog has shown up. Poster above, you like wolves so much, could you be a wolf that was domesticated into a dog?"

"They say wolves can't be domesticated, so they must have been dogs from the moment they were born."

"The blogger uses a poem to state his convictions. Well written, and even better done."

"Go, blogger! You be the Xuan Niao, and we netizens will be the Gusha Immortals and the Goddess of the Luo River from the poem, supporting you and cheering you on online!"

In just two days, this article posting the poem actually broke 50,000 clicks.

The current situation was that the traditional media was split half-and-half between support and opposition. But on the internet, aside from the somewhat abstract portal websites, public opinion on other sites was almost completely one-sided.

This was because in traditional media and on portal sites, the author and publisher of *Wolf Totem* could use their connections to create positive public opinion. But the vast majority of netizens wouldn't listen to them!

In the field of mass communication, the weak are inherently seen as righteous. People put themselves in their shoes and subconsciously side with the underdog.

Chen Guiliang was very much the underdog. His age, qualifications, background, resources... all were inferior to his opponent's. In the eyes of the vast majority of netizens, he was a fearless warrior charging at an evil dragon.

This was especially true for the cohort of "educated youth" who had been sent down to the grasslands. Most of them were furious after reading the book, and they flooded the forums with posts to reveal the truth.

There were 120 people in the same group of educated youth sent down with the author. The vast majority were still alive, and quite a few had become successful and influential.

Writer Jiang, who had always proclaimed "no photos, no recordings, no interviews," had not deigned to pay any attention to Chen Guiliang. But the voices of the educated youth cohort broke through his defenses.

Just a few days later, Writer Jiang took the initiative to contact the media.

"This book is written entirely based on my 11 years of experience living in the pastoral regions. There is absolutely no fabrication. The recent questions and attacks on my work from the media are one-sided and untrue..."

"The herdsmen's feelings towards wolves are not the deep-seated hatred and utter detestation that the objectors claim. Wolves are a main force in ecological conservation, an important animal for balancing various relationships on the grassland. It is the claims of certain people that twist the facts!"

"I can say with certainty that all the material is real, and all the details have sources. Some are from my personal experience, and others were obtained through personal investigation..."

"The most authoritative judges of this book shouldn't be the educated youth, but the local herdsmen. Those educated youth don't understand the situation. They have agendas and biases, and even have problems with their comprehension..."

"On the grasslands, I was deeply baptized by the spirit of the wolf totem. For thousands of years, the wolf totem has always been the totem of the grassland peoples..."

From the content of these interviews with Writer Jiang, it was clear that he had never taken Chen Guiliang seriously from beginning to end. What was a young kid? He wasn't even worthy of a personal response.

It was only those educated youth from back then that made Writer Jiang panic!

Because many of those educated youth held significant power in the real world and knew all his old secrets.

As for the questions raised by Chen Guiliang and other scholars, Writer Jiang chose to avoid them all. The reporters also deliberately refrained from asking, because they had been invited by him in the first place.

"Your book sales have skyrocketed these past few days! Especially on Dangdang, Amazon Joyo, and 99read. The total online sales for the last three days are close to 40,000 copies. This is online, selling over ten thousand copies a day!" Li Xunhuan said excitedly over the phone.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about *Wolf Totem*?"

Li Xunhuan said, "Its daily online sales have dropped severely. Offline sales don't seem to be greatly affected. But it's hard to say, offline sales figures can be faked."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Is there anything else you need me to do?"

"No need for any more moves," Li Xunhuan said. "*Wolf Totem* had too much marketing last year, and its content angered a lot of people. It was bound to run into trouble sooner or later. Now that you've jumped in and stirred things up, others will naturally follow suit, and some of them are very big players. *People's Daily* and *Guangming Daily* have gone quiet now. Only *Southern Metropolis Daily* and Phoenix Television are still being stubborn. When titans clash, we need to stay far away."

Chen Guiliang said, "I still need to finish my analysis of *Wolf Totem* on my blog. I have to see things through to the end."

"Do as you like," Li Xunhuan said, taking the chance to press for the manuscript. "If you have that kind of time, you'd be better off writing more of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*, Volume Four."

Just as Li Xunhuan had said, Chen Guiliang had already lit the fire and didn't need to make any more big moves.

Experts from all sides entered the fray one after another!

Over the past two days, the fiercest critic of *Wolf Totem* had become the grassland-ethnic writer Guo Xuebo, who directly claimed that "promoting the wolf spirit is an anti-human, fascist ideology."

Guo Xuebo had ample reason to open fire!

First, he was a bona fide member of a grassland ethnicity, so he could attack the topic as harshly as he wanted without any repercussions.

Second, he was a believer in Shamanism and Buddhism, and *Wolf Totem* insulted his faith.

Third, he was a researcher of grassland history, culture, and environmental literature, and *Wolf Totem* was causing chaos in his academic field.

Fourth, he had published a book four years ago titled *Wolf Child of the Great Desert*. At first glance, it seemed to have a similar theme to *Wolf Totem*, but its ideas, principles, and overall magnanimity left *Wolf Totem* in the dust.

But after *Wolf Totem* became a massive hit, pirates began aggressively promoting *Wolf Child of the Great Desert*. Some called it a sister work, some called it a sequel, and some even changed the author's name!

How could Guo Xuebo tolerate that?

Now, a legitimate publisher had approached Guo Xuebo, planning to republish *Wolf Child of the Great Desert*.

Whether it was to sell books and make money or to vent his personal frustrations, Guo Xuebo was going to tear into *Wolf Totem*!

Lao Gui said *Wolf Totem* encouraged Chinese people to be traitors.

Guo Xuebo said *Wolf Totem* promoted fascism and was an anti-human book.

Chen Guiliang had just hung up the phone when Li Xunhuan called again. "The publisher working with Guo Xuebo wants to invite you to write a preface for the reprint of *Wolf Child of the Great Desert*."

This collaboration...

Chen Guiliang didn't agree rashly, instead saying, "Let me read the book first."

"Okay," Li Xunhuan said. "Then I'll give them your phone number. The publisher will send you the book in a couple of days."

Tucking his phone into his pocket, Chen Guiliang rode his bicycle to class.

The semester had already started.

Chen Guiliang's exam results from last semester: out of 14 courses, he had failed 6.

Chen Guiliang was actually quite pleased with this, grateful to the professors of the other 8 courses for going easy on him.

He had thought he would fail more than 10.

As he sped along on his bike, even before he entered the academic building, a student recognized him and shouted from the roadside, "Chen Guiliang, you're awesome!"

Calling him awesome was, of course, because of this war of words.

Writer Jiang's old secrets had all been exposed. Anyone paying attention to the matter knew which side to support. Well... with the exception of certain humanoid creatures.

This class was "History of Chinese Civilization," a mandatory foundational course for the Yuanpei Program.

When Chen Guiliang arrived at the large lecture hall, he was immediately greeted with a warm welcome from his Yuanpei classmates. This kind of reception far surpassed the one he got when news of him starting a company spread.

The things students admire are different from those of adults!

Professor Zhu clapped his hands from the lectern. "Welcome back, our hero."

"Hahahaha!"

"Clap, clap, clap, clap..."

The whole class laughed and applauded together.

Professor Zhu added, "It would have been even more perfect if, in the process of your critique of *Wolf Totem*, you had omitted the philistine act of leeching off its fame to sell your own book."

"Hahaha!"

Another wave of laughter erupted from the class.

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

This Professor Zhu always spoke with cutting insight and without holding back.

Professor Zhu was an art researcher, and in the "History of Chinese Civilization" course, he was responsible for the section on ancient Chinese art.

The man's thinking was somewhat contradictory.

He highly admired ancient Chinese art and was also dedicated to the modernization of Chinese art, believing that artistic modernization was not a Western patent.

At the same time, he lacked some cultural confidence, always inadvertently revealing a desire for Chinese art to gain Western recognition. He cared too much about the opinions of Westerners.

On one hand, he wanted to protect and develop traditional Chinese art, believing that economic development would be more conducive to this protection; on the other hand, he felt that the protection and development of traditional art had become overly commercialized, which was a destruction of traditional art.

He was proud yet unconfident, able to see the problems but not knowing how to solve them.

His impression of Chen Guiliang was much the same. He both admired Chen Guiliang's courage in being the first to attack *Wolf Totem* and disdained his ulterior motive of deliberately leeching off its fame.

Of course, Professor Zhu's lectures were brilliant. Even people who didn't understand art could listen with great interest. And he could always hit upon the crux of an issue with a single sentence.

Before the class ended, Chen Guiliang received a text message.

Mi Lan, who had participated in the New Concept Writing Competition with him, sent him a message: "Someone is doing promotions on the Fudan campus, going door to door in the dorms with gifts. As long as you register on 5q Campus Network, you get a small gift. Your Xiaonei Wang has a competitor."

"Thanks for the heads-up," Chen Guiliang replied.

(End of this chapter)
